subject: Negotiation: Uptime credits, on-call coverage & packaging options
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@brightcart.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Velez <elena.velez@brightcart.com>, procurement@brightcart.com
Date: 2027-05-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Reviewing SLA options — can we tighten response windows?

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the proposal packet — useful baseline. Two quick asks from our side as we align with legal & ops: 

1) Can we get a concrete example of how uptime credits would be calculated for a blended multi-region deployment (us-east + eu-west)? Our CFO wants the worst-case exposure quantified.
2) Can the P1 response window be tightened from 1 hour to 45 minutes for the Premium tier if we commit to a 12-month committed spend?
3) On escalation coverage: we need a named escalation contact during US business hours + 24/7 on-call for P1 for the first 90 days of launch.

Attached our launch timeline and a one-pager on procurement constraints. If you can draft a short mutual action plan with those asks, we can fast-track.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Operations, BrightCart
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@brightcart.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-15T14:06:00Z
Subject: Re: Reviewing SLA options — can we tighten response windows?

Sanjay — thanks for the clear asks. Quick response while I pull exact numbers with finance: 

- Uptime credits: we can do a blended calculation for multi-region: per-region SLA is measured independently; credits are applied pro-rata on affected region capacity. I attached a workbook that walks through a sample outage scenario for your us-east + eu-west split. That will give your CFO a worst-case (both regions impacted) and a more likely partial-impact number.

- P1 window: we can commit to 45 minutes for Premium if BrightCart signs a 12-month commit and agrees to a modest 10% uplift on the monthly committed capacity compared to the baseline quote. This helps us allocate a dedicated on-call rotation for your tenant.

- Escalation contacts: we can provide a named ERT (engineer in the rotation) for US business hours + a 24/7 on-call rotation for P1 for the first 90 days at no extra charge as a ramp concession. After 90 days we propose switching to the standard premium on-call retainer (option to keep gratis coverage for an additional fee).

I'll loop in Marissa on pricing specifics and Ben on the dedicated rotation commitments. Draft MAP coming shortly.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@brightcart.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-16T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Reviewing SLA options — can we tighten response windows?

Sanjay — a few pricing specifics from my side:

Summary of options we can propose formally in the MAP: 

A) Standard Premium: 1-hour P1 / blended uptime SLA credits as-is / 24x7 on-call retainer optional (baseline pricing).

B) Premium+ (12-month commit): 45-minute P1 + named US business-hours ERT + 90-day 24x7 on-call ramp included. Pricing = baseline * (commit discount factor) + 10% uplift to reserve capacity for the rotation. Net effect is ~6% off list when amortized across committed spend vs monthly.

C) Hybrid credit model: reduce the committed uplift to 5%, but we apply a stricter credit multiplier on severity (i.e., larger credits for multi-region full outages) that protects BrightCart's downside. This option shifts risk to Redwood's balance sheet for a higher potential credit payout.

Attachments: redwood-sla-options-2027-05-15.pdf (detailed table) and an example credit calc (.xlsx).

If you prefer, we can structure the 45-minute SLA as a time-limited pilot: first 6 months at the pilot SLA with an executive review at T+4 months. That reduces long-term exposure on both sides.

Would love to hear which approach aligns better with procurement and finance.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@brightcart.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Velez <elena.velez@brightcart.com>, procurement@brightcart.com
Date: 2027-05-17T11:33:00Z
Subject: Re: Reviewing SLA options — can we tighten response windows?

Marissa/Tessa — thanks, that helps. A few follow-ups from procurement and finance after reviewing the attachments: 

- Procurement prefers a capped credit exposure rather than an open-ended multiplier (they worry about indemnity on extreme events). Can Redwood propose a credit cap as a % of monthly committed spend per region?
- Finance would like the 10% uplift option modeled as an annualized delta ($) so we can compare to the cost of hiring our own standby rotation. If the annual cost delta is < hiring one FTE equivalent, that’s very attractive.
- On the pilot: BrightCart is open to the 6-month pilot for 45-minute P1, but we need a clause that ensures the pilot SLA is maintained during the pilot (no backslide) and a formal executive review at month 4 with the option to extend or terminate.

Can you put those points into the MAP and share a DocuSign link for the pilot amendment? We aim to present to our CFO by next Wednesday.

Regards,
Sanjay
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@brightcart.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-18T16:48:00Z
Subject: Re: Reviewing SLA options — can we tighten response windows?

Sanjay — attaching a draft MAP and pilot amendment (DocuSign link below). Key commitments we added per your asks: 

- Credit cap: we propose a cap equal to 150% of that region's monthly committed spend for any single incident (this limits legal exposure while still providing meaningful downside protection).
- Annualized uplift model: redwood has modeled the 10% uplift as an annual delta in the attached workbook — in most BrightCart-like profiles the uplift is ~40–55k/year vs hiring a dedicated on-call engineer, but exact result depends on your usage pattern.
- Pilot clause: 6-month pilot for 45-minute P1 with a mandatory executive review at month 4; during the pilot we guarantee the SLA and maintain the free 90-day 24x7 ramp in parallel. Termination mechanics and transition to baseline are documented in the amendment.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/xyz/BRGHT-SLA-0421
MAP (attached): mutual-action-plan-brightcart-2027-05-18.pdf

If this looks good I can send the DocuSign envelope to procurement and the CFO. We can also schedule the executive review now for week 4 of the pilot.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-sla-options-2027-05-15.pdf (PDF), uptime-credit-workbook.xlsx (Excel)
